transcript: Last night I saw the refuge plays, a world premiere co production between roundabout and New York Theater Workshop. The show is still in previews, but as of last night, it's a whopping three hours and 45 minutes long with two intermissions. We're following the history of one family through multiple generations, and the stories told in reverse chronological order. This is a huge play that explores a lot of questions, but the themes I was mostly thinking about while I was watching were generational expectations and responsibility, the costs and rewards that come with maintaining a family unit, and the concept of home, how we define it or don't define it in relation to specific people or places. There are 10 characters across the entire play, some of whom are present in more than one act. But overall, the show really feels like three distinct pieces, each with their own sub themes, styles of dialogue, and mood. This play covers a lot of ground. It has moments of brilliance, poignants and comedy, and other moments that felt a little slow or forced in terms of exposition. So overall, it's definitely still a work in progress, but I was really impressed with how ambitious it was and the incredible understudy who went on for one of the main roles, partial script in hand. Her performance in Act 3 specifically was well worth waiting for. With that, another play Bill for my collection.
